reasons: Lake identity records the case as United States v. Timothy Carpenter in the 6th Cir. with year 2019 and expected_citation_found=true.
Lake official/display citation is 926 F.3d 313, matching the page's reporter citation; lake has no parallel or neutral citation.
The opinion identifies the remand question as whether the FBI agents who obtained Carpenter's CSLI acted in good faith.
The analysis applies Leon/Krull good-faith principles and concludes the agents reasonably relied on the SCA, so a Key home role on The Good-Faith Exception is supported.
The opinion states that the Supreme Court disagreed with the prior no-search holding and that the Government's collection of Carpenter's CSLI was a Fourth Amendment search requiring a warrant.
The conclusion states that the acquisition violated the Fourth Amendment but suppression was properly denied because the FBI agents relied in good faith on the SCA when they obtained the data.
Treatment/currency is outside Lens A; no treatment-law defect is raised.
Disclosed identity evidence identifies a Sixth Circuit court-of-appeals case: court=6th Cir., court_level=coa, circuit=ca6.
